(By Sri. P.M. Venkataramana, Adv)
 :JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 02.06.2022 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Anil Kumar Saxena due to the impact of the accident.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of deceased Anil Kumar Saxena who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 02.06.2022 due to the negligence of the rider of the respondent's motorcycle.

It is submitted that on 02.06.2022 at about 8.10 a.m., deceased Anil Kumar Saxena was trying to cross the road near Pipe line road, Karumariyamma Temple, T.Dasarahalli, carefully, cautiously and observing traffic rules, at that time,
the respondent's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KC-9330 which was ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, endangering to human life and dashed against the Anil Kumar Saxena resulting in the accident.

Immediately after the accident Anil Kumar Saxena was shifted to Prakriya hospital,
but he died while under treatment.

Consequently, on 02.06.2022 a FIR No.0096/2022 was registered with the Peenya Traffic Police station under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279 and 304(A) of SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4386/2022 IPC against the rider of the Renu Saxena vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155853065/
2 motorcycle.

sentences.text: The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 65 years and working as Tutor / retired government employee and was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. and Rs.44,000/- towards pension at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsels and filed their Written Statements to the main petition.

Respondent No.1 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.1 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KC-9330 SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4386/2022 in favour of the respondent No.2.
Further stated that deceased himself was tort feasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
It is submitted that the rider of the offending motorcycle was not having valid driving license.

The age, occupation and the income of the deceased and manner of the accident and vehicle involved in the accident and the cause of death are denied and the petitioners are called upon to prove the same.

It is submitted that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary,
unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The present petition is not maintainable either in law or facts.
This court has no territorial jurisdiction to try this petition.
The manner of the accident is denied.
The accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased himself and not due to the rash or negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
It is submitted that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4386/2022 excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.

Hence,
on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-

REASONS 7. Point No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Enfield motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KC-9330 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle).

In this regard the PW.4 got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 02.06.2022 at about 8.10 a.m. his father was crossing the Pipeline road, near Karumariyamma temple, T. Dasarahalli and at that time all of sudden the rider of the motorcycle came in a rash and negligent manner in high speed and dashed the deceased and he succumbed to the injuries.

In support of the same, PW.1 has produced Ex.P1 which is the Complaint and Ex.P2 is the charge sheet which discloses that after investigation the charge sheet has filed against the rider of the motorcycle for offences under Sec.279 and 304A of IPC and it is stated that the rider of the motorcycle dashed to the pedestrian from behind resulting in the accident.
As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is subject to cross- examination and in the cross-examination PW.1 has admitted that he has not seen the accident.

He has deposed that she along with her deceased Renu Saxena vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155853065/
4 father were going to drop her son to school bus and denied that the accident took place when the deceased was crossing the road and stated that they were only standing beside the road nor the cross the road.

sentences.text: Except the said suggestion SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4386/2022 nothing much is elicted in the cross-examination of PW.1 to disprove the manner of the accident.
Hence, in the absence of any rebuttal evidence it can be concluded that the accident took place due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending motorcycle.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the "Affirmative ".
9. Point No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased Anil Kumar Saxena.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P7 to 11 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners and deceased.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

Hence, they have a right to apply for compensation due to death of Anil Kumar Saxena in RTA.
10.

In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Reliance can also be placed on the dictum SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4386/2022 in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender (2020), wherein it was expounded that "major married and earning sons of the deceased,
being legal representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not."

sentences.text:
11. Though the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased,
being the legal representatives of deceased Anil Kumar Saxena have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Anil Kumar Saxena and also they have proved that the death of the Anil Kumar Saxena has been caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

12. Point No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the SCCH 15 11 MVC No.4386/2022 head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 65 years.
Ex.P-11 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 04.03.1955.
The alleged accident has taken place on 02.06.2022.
Hence, by considering Ex.P11, the age of the deceased is taken as 67 years.
13. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a Tutor and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased.

Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual Renu Saxena vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155853065/
5 income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Renu Saxena vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,500X 12= 1,86,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,86,000/-.

14. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4386/2022 v.
DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4386/2022 v.
DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4386/2022 the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.

The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the Renu Saxena vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155853065/
6 deceased."

sentences.text:
Moving forward with the Point of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, there is no addition salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased age is more than 60 years.
15.

sentences.text: At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife and married daughters and son.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4386/2022 number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was pleased to hold that where the number of dependents of family members is 4 to 6,  th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
16. In this Petition, the deceased was aged 67 years at the time of accident.
"There should be no addition after 60 years.".
The income of the deceased was taken at Rs.15,500/- p.m..
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 5.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to held that where the number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6, th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
17. After deducting th of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.15,500/- it comes to Rs.11,625/- (15,500/- - 3,875/-) and multiplier applied is 5, (Rs.11,625/- x 12 x 5 = 6,97,500/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4386/2022 Rs.6,97,500/- towards loss of dependency.
18. Medical expenses: The petitioners have produced Ex.
P4 - Medical bills total 17 in nos.

and hence the petitioners are entitled an amount of Rs.3,57,433/- under this head.
19. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses' In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KC-9330.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.

22. Point No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,84,833/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,84,833/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and SCCH 15 19 MVC No.4386/2022 interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 85% to the Petitioner No.1 After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 to 4 is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be released to them by way of E- payment and after their proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH 15 20 MVC No.4386/2022 Draw Award accordingly.

ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 to 4 is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be released to them by way of E- payment and after their proper identification.
